whatIs: NameThatUI is a visual dictionary of interfaces: you describe a UI element in your own words and it gives you back its real name, its API symbol and a prompt ready to paste into a coding agent. It has entries for macOS and the web, an option to view a random entry and comparison guides across technologies.
It's a good fit when you know what something looks like but not what it's called, and you need the right term to search for it, ask for it in a prompt or implement it.
uses: Finding out that the panel that slides in from an edge is called a sheet or drawer before you go looking for libraries.
Getting the exact name of an element so you can ask a coding agent for it in a precise prompt.
Looking up the equivalent of a component across AppKit, SwiftUI and the web when porting an interface.
caveats: The catalog is limited, about 90 entries, and covers only macOS and the web.
The name it returns is a reference: check it against your framework's documentation, because each library may call the same component something different.
The site shows ads for other products by its authors and offers sponsorship slots.
pricingNote: You can use it without signing up or paying.
idealFor: Anyone who knows what they want on screen but not what it's called.
